comparator.name: Psychology / Psychologie
comparator.sourceNotes: The current official curriculum accounts for 180 EC as three 60-EC years. Year one is a broad common foundation: Introductory Psychology and Brain & Cognition (12 EC), Research Methods & Statistics (12), Developmental Psychology (6), Work and Organisational Psychology & Social Psychology (12), Clinical Psychology & Neuropsychology (12), Behavioural Data Science (3), and the First-year Thesis (3); the separately described academic-skills tutorials and research participation carry no stated EC and are therefore not added to the 180-EC reconstruction. The first half of year two contains Scientific and Statistical Reasoning (9), Psychological Communication (3), Psychological Research (12), and Fundamentals of Psychology (6). Its second half is one 30-EC specialisation. The detailed numbered curriculum lists Brain and Cognition first, so it is selected as a neutral official-order tie-break for this generic target; Clinical Neuropsychology is Dutch-only, while the other six specialisations are available across the English and Dutch tracks. Year three contains specialisation-linked Methods & Statistics (6), a Bachelor's Thesis (12), two 6-EC current-topics choices, and a genuine 30-EC optional profile comprising a second specialisation, minor, exchange, or individually selected courses. The current page is prospective and does not guarantee one fixed entrant-cohort timetable.

Studies memory, attention, executive function and cognitive control at an advanced level.
Studies psychological processes in health, illness and medical settings.

Studies perceptual processing and motor action as mechanisms of cognition.
Studies mental disorders from infancy to adulthood and their biopsychosocial explanations.
Examines cognitive and social development over the lifespan.
Practices research synthesis, effect-size reasoning and evaluation of psychological evidence.
Studies youth resilience and social-emotional support in relation to extremism.
Analyses social trust and the civil sphere as contexts for group behaviour.
Tests persuasion, framing and cognitive shortcuts that shape behaviour change.
Examines agency, selfhood and free will as concepts behind psychological interpretations of action.

alternatives.label: Psychology, brain & cognition
alternatives.concept: A psychology programme combining broad behavioural, developmental, social and clinical foundations with an emphasis on brain, cognition, perception, memory, language and empirical research. UCR cannot reproduce UvA's dedicated 30-EC specialisation, professional practicals or supervised psychology thesis.
alternatives.labelReason: The schedule covers the broad psychology core and sustains a brain-and-cognition emphasis without claiming equivalence to UvA's formal specialisation.
progression: Introductory brain, biomedical, social and method courses precede formally dependent advanced courses; every assigned term is offered.

alternatives.label: Clinical, developmental & mental-health psychology
alternatives.concept: A psychologically grounded route emphasising development, psychopathology, clinical assessment, health, public health, biomedical mechanisms and ethics. It does not constitute clinical training or professional qualification.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed programme combines development, mental health, assessment, health and research, and the label avoids implying professional qualification.
progression: All formal brain and biomedical prerequisites are earlier; development and methods precede the advanced clinical work; assigned terms are offered.
alternatives.distinctness: The clinical path substitutes population health, pharmacology, biomedical disease mechanisms and healthcare ethics for communication, philosophy-of-mind and social-persuasion emphases in the broad route; this is a substantive change in what mental-health evidence and support students study.

alternatives.label: Social & organisational psychology
alternatives.concept: A social-behaviour route focused on social influence, group processes, motivation, leadership, diversity, negotiation and organisational communication, grounded in psychology and empirical research.
alternatives.labelReason: Psychology, sociology, leadership and communication appear throughout the completed schedule, so a combined label describes it more accurately than organisational psychology alone.
progression: Research Methods & Statistics precedes advanced leadership coursework; Introduction to Brain & Behavior precedes dependent psychology courses, and all terms are offered.
alternatives.distinctness: This path changes the upper-year curriculum toward organisational behaviour, leadership, diversity, social influence and applied communication rather than the broad cognitive and clinical/health sequences in the other routes.
traceOverrides: Examines agency, selfhood and free will as concepts behind psychological interpretations of action.

candidates.label: Psychological methods and behavioural data
candidates.reason: The methods direction is well supported, but the three-alternative maximum is reached; quantitative and experimental methods already run through the included programmes.

candidates.label: Clinical neuropsychology
candidates.reason: This Dutch-only specialisation is supported, but the three-alternative cap is reached and its brain, cognition and clinical interests are represented across the selected and clinical paths.

routeSelection.basis: The generic target permits seven formal specialisations. The detailed numbered curriculum lists Brain and Cognition first; no official source identifies a default. This choice is fixed independently of UCR fit. Clinical Neuropsychology is Dutch-only and is not used for the bilingual generic target.

selection.assessment: The selected Brain and Cognition pathway and two distinct feasible clinical/developmental and social/organisational directions answer the strongest formal specialisation clusters. Psychological Methods and Dutch-only Clinical Neuropsychology were assessed separately; three alternatives is the maximum.

notes.text: UCR can combine psychology, cognition, biology, sociology, research, communication and leadership, but it does not reproduce UvA Psychology's dedicated disciplinary sequence, formal 30-EC specialisations, psychological practical training or specialisation-linked 12-EC thesis. Clinical courses do not amount to clinical training or qualification.
